rows.title: Pest

text_1.eng: A pest is any insect, disease, or animal that harms your crops and livestock.

rows.text_1: A pest is any insect, disease, or animal that harms your crops and livestock.

rows.title: Pest Management

text_1.eng: Pest management involves using natural and chemical tools to monitor and control pests before they cause damage.

text_2.eng: The goal is to protect your crops and livestock while keeping your farm healthy and profitable.

rows.title: Soft Bodied Pests

text_1.eng: Soft-bodied pests are insects with soft outer layers that damage crops by feeding on plant sap and tissues.

section_1_extra_text.eng:
* Bore holes in plants
 * Harm roots
 * Steal nutrients from your plants.

rows.title: Hard Bodied Pests

text_1.eng: Hard bodied pests have a tough outer shell or exoskeleton that protects them from the environment, predators, and even some chemicals.

section_1_extra_text.eng:
* Chew leaves, fruits or grains
 * Makes holes into the heart of the plant 
 * Feed on and damage roots
 * Transmit harmful bacteria and diseases

rows.title: How to Control Pests

text_1.eng: To protect your crops from harmful insects naturally, these simple, safe, and affordable methods will help you manage pests using resources already available in your home and farm.

rows.text_1: To protect your crops from harmful insects naturally, these simple, safe, and affordable methods will help you manage pests using resources already available in your home and farm.

rows.title: Cultural Control

text_1.eng: This involves using farming practices and field management to prevent and manage pests.

media_transcript.eng:
Examples of Cultural Practices are:
 1. Rotate crops and plant at the right time.
 2. Grow pest-repellent crops (e.g., onions).
 3. Harvest on time before pests attack.
 4. Use healthy seeds, fertilizers, and resistant crop varieties.
 5. Remove weeds and diseased plants.

rows.title: Biological Control

text_1.eng: It involves using natural enemies like predators, parasites, and pathogens to manage and control pest populations.

media_transcript.eng: As farmers, we can use nature’s own army to protect our harvests through biological control. This simply means encouraging the "good insects" to fight pests for us. For example, ladybirds feed on destructive aphids, wasps hunt down harmful insects, and a farm cat will eat the rats in your grain stores.

rows.title: Physical Control

section_1_text.eng:
* Use **scarecrows** to keep birds away.
 * Set traps and use nets, screens, or fences.
 * Pick pests off by hand.

rows.title: Botanical Methods

text_1.eng: Involves using plant extracts as natural insecticides to control pests.

text_2.eng: Ensure you watch videos in the ***'Practical Section'*** on how to make these plant extracts and the ingredents used.

media_transcript.eng: We can also protect our crops using natural, homemade biopesticides like wood ash, soap, an ash brew, or hot pepper instead of expensive chemicals. To invite more of these helpful insects to your farm, simply plant flowers around your fields. By combining natural enemies with simple homemade solutions, you save money, protect your soil, and let nature work for you.

section_1_text.eng: These plants have chemicals that make crops taste bad to pests, so they stay away.

section_1_extra_text.eng:
* Neem plant
 * Tithonia
 * Aloe vera
 * Tephrosia.

rows.title: Proper Storage

section_1_text.eng:
* Dry maize and cereals properly to make them too hard for weevils to attack.
 * Store in hermetic bags or silos to prevent pests.
